newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Bonos were higher at the close on Wednesday but off today's new high of 109.93, with the market warily eyeing the U.S. Federal Reserve's Open Market Committee meeting, dealers said.

They were a little disappointed by the failure of December futures contract to breach the 110 level, but added that the underlying tone of the Spanish market was still very positive in anticipation of benign October inflation, scheduled tomorrow.
"I guess we can reach the 110 level and then we'll likely see profit-taking," a dealer in Madrid said. Chart analysts pegged resistance at 110.12.
A week ago a Reuter poll forecast the October CPI at 0.2 pct month-on-month and at 3.6 percent year-on-year. But analysts and dealers were more positive today.
"My forecast is lower. I guess the Spanish CPI could show some correlation with the Italian, which was lower in October," told Riccardo Barbieri, a Morgan Stanley economist in London.
U.S. October PPI, which pleased T-bonds, didn't blaze a trail to bonos -- they found a shine all of their own.
Proof of this was in the 10-year spread over Bunds, which fell to 153 basis points from 155 this morning, while the differential over Italian Btps was locked at 30 bps.
